Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Ley 14/2021, de 11 de octubre and Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, implementing the Fourth EU Anti-Money Laundering Directive (Directive (EU) 2015/849) and subsequent amendments (Fifth and Sixth AML Directives). UBO register established under Real Decreto-ley 7/2021, de 27 de abril, transposing the Fifth AML Directive (Directive (EU) 2018/843), creating the 'Registro de Titularidad Real' — 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (S.L.)' governed by Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC).
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

Under Article 9 LSC, the registered office (domicilio social) must be located in Spanish territory — specifically, the place where the central administration or principal establishment is actually located. A 'virtual office' (i.e., purely administrative correspondence address without personnel, equipment, or activity presence) is NOT permissible for a biotech/nanoparticle manufacturing SL given the industry's requirement for a physical establishment, appropriate laboratory and GMP compliant facilities, and Spanish tax substance expectations under the anti-abuse doctrine. A 'registered office service' providing a physical commercial address with a physical presence, attended staff, and mailbox handling may provisionally satisfy the statutory requirement only during the pre-incorporation and initial licensing phase, but the tax authorities and the Mercantile Registry presume absence of substance if no physical economic activity is conducted at that address. The ISIC 2100 scope (nanoparticle microfluidic encapsulation of mRNA lipid emulsions) triggers mandatory pharmaceutical GMP inspection and requires a dedicated clean-room laboratory facility with manufacturing space; therefore, the company must lease or acquire real premises permitting organism/biologic containment and environmental compliance. A post-incorporation 'factual domicile mismatch' between registered office and the actual principal place of business is sanctionable and may result in the nullity of corporate deeds and tax reassessments.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

The relevant Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) under the Ministry of Justice; the Central Mercantile Registry issues the name-clearance certificate.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), principally Articles 4, 19-23, 28-30, 32, 33, 62, 63, 73-79, 210-242 and 253-279; Royal Decree 1784/1996, approving the Mercantile Registry Regulations.

Formation / constitutional filings

Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) filed for registration with the relevant Provincial Mercantile Registry, together with the certified company name certificate and tax identification documentation.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 53 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

The statutory minimum capital for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1.00. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. While share capital remains below EUR 3,000, the company must allocate at least 20% of annual profit to legal reserve until capital plus reserve reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholders have statutory supplementary liability on liquidation for the difference between EUR 3,000 and subscribed capital. No general escrow account is required; a bank certificate evidencing cash contribution may be used, although the founders may dispense with that certificate and accept statutory liability under Article 62.

Funding & unlock path: Before operation, obtain or file the municipal opening/activity authorization and demonstrate compliance with the Technical Building Code, Royal Decree 513/2017 on fire-protection installations, applicable industrial fire-safety rules, and regional fire authority requirements. Complete structural, seismic where applicable, pressure-equipment, electrical, chemical-storage, and load inspections. Implement occupational risk prevention under Law 31/1995, including workplace risk assessment, emergency planning, biological and chemical-agent controls, worker training, medical surveillance, and coordination with external prevention services.

Paid-in capital rule: The statutory minimum capital for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1.00. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. While share capital remains below EUR 3,000, the company must allocate at least 20% of annual profit to legal reserve until capital plus reserve reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholders have statutory supplementary liability on liquidation for the difference between EUR 3,000 and subscribed capital. No general escrow account is required; a bank certificate evidencing cash contribution may be used, although the founders may dispense with that certificate and accept statutory liability under Article 62.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
The Board resolves that the Company accept and ratify the subscriptions and full payment of the shares recorded in the incorporation deed and approve the resulting shareholding ledger. The registered office is adopted at [full Spanish address], with authority granted to the managing director to notify the Mercantile Registry and tax authorities of any permitted change. [Name] is appointed sole director/managing director, and [name], if applicable, is appointed attorney with the powers set out in Schedule 1. The officers shall arrange tax registration, accounting books, beneficial-owner records, banking facilities, insurance, and all applications required for industrial, environmental, pharmaceutical, occupational, and fire-safety compliance.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

The competent autonomous-community industrial authority for the facility location, coordinated with the Spanish Agency for Medicines and Medical Devices (Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios, AEMPS). For a medicinal-product or vaccine-adjuvant manufacturing operation, AEMPS manufacturing authorization and Good Manufacturing Practice compliance are required where the product falls within the medicinal-product regime.

Category: Authorization for the manufacture, import, or distribution of medicinal products for human use (autorización de fabricación o importación de medicamentos de uso humano), issued under Royal Legislative Decree 1/2015 and applicable AEMPS procedures; additionally, an autonomous-community industrial activity or installation registration and municipal activity/opening licence or responsible declaration may be required.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

For a newly formed Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the legal representative obtains a provisional NIF before filing the incorporation deed, then files Form 036 (declaración censal) with AEAT within one month of registration in the Mercantile Registry. The filing must attach the notarized deed of incorporation, tax ID documentation for all shareholders, identification of the appointed director(s), and proof of registered office. AEAT issues the definitive NIF (letter-prefixed, e.g., B99999999) and assigns the Spanish VAT number once the activity commencement declaration is accepted. Where the parent or beneficial owner is a foreign non-resident entity, a fiscal representative (representante fiscal) must be appointed and the additional non-resident census registration (Form 036 in the non-resident register) must be completed, with apostilled/certified corporate documents and, if not in Spanish, sworn translations. No separate TIN application is required for an SL beyond the NIF/VAT census dossier.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation – A Spanish SL is a corporation resident in Spain and subject to corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at 25% on worldwide profits; it is not a pass-through entity and no entity classification check-the-box election is available. Non-resident entities are subject to Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) on Spanish-source income only. — For a newly formed Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the legal representative obtains a provisional NIF before filing the incorporation deed, then files Form 036 (declaración censal) with AEAT within one month of registration in the Mercantile Registry. The filing must attach the notarized deed of incorporation, tax ID documentation for all shareholders, identification of the appointed director(s), and proof of registered office. AEAT issues the definitive NIF (letter-prefixed, e.g., B99999999) and assigns the Spanish VAT number once the activity commencement declaration is accepted. Where the parent or beneficial owner is a foreign non-resident entity, a fiscal representative (representante fiscal) must be appointed and the additional non-resident census registration (Form 036 in the non-resident register) must be completed, with apostilled/certified corporate documents and, if not in Spanish, sworn translations. No separate TIN application is required for an SL beyond the NIF/VAT census dossier.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation – A Spanish SL is a corporation resident in Spain and subject to corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at 25% on worldwide profits; it is not a pass-through entity and no entity classification check-the-box election is available. Non-resident entities are subject to Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) on Spanish-source income only.

Available election forms

No check-the-box election is recognized. Under Spanish corporate income tax law, taxpayers may elect: (a) the consolidated tax group regime (arts. 67-73 LIS) where the parent holds the required direct/indirect control and all resident group members are included; (b) participation exemption application for foreign-source dividends and capital gains (art. 21 LIS); (c) special 15% reduced CIT rate for newly created entities in their first two profitable years (art. 29.1 LIS); (d) the ETVE holding regime for qualifying foreign securities; and (e) the Patent Box regime for qualified intangible assets (art. 23 LIS). Hybrid mismatch consequences are mandatory statutory adjustments under arts. 15 bis and 21 bis LIS, not elective safe harbours.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general registration threshold. Any person carrying out taxable supplies in Spain must register before commencing activities; however, for intra-Union distance sales by EU suppliers, the threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year (below which VAT may remain in the EU country of establishment unless an OSS election is made). There is no exemption threshold for export-oriented manufacturers; VAT registration is mandatory to claim input VAT deductions and issue export invoices.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods from mainland Spain to third countries outside EU VAT territory are exempt with credit at 0% under art. 21 LIVA where the goods leave the EU within prescribed deadlines, evidenced by the customs export declaration (DUA) and shipping documentation. Intra-Community supplies of goods to a customer holding a valid Spanish/EU VIES VAT number are also 0% rated under art. 25 LIVA and require recapitulative statement (RECAP) listing; services connected with export goods or to non-established recipients (e.g., tolling, logistics, technical documentation for the liposomal vaccine adjuvant) may be zero-rated or exempt under arts. 21-22 LIVA if the direct benefit of the service is tied to the export and the prescribed proof is retained. Manufacturers exporting pharmaceutical/vaccine adjuvant products must be the customs exporter of record or have secured export agency in the customs declaration.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo) validated by Spanish Customs or exit customs office
  • Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document evidencing physical departure from EU customs territory
  • Commercial invoice and packing list matching the export declaration
  • Inward Remittance Certificate / bank statement proving export payment repatriation within 180 days
  • Intra-EU VIES number confirmation and RECAP entry (for intra-community zero-rated supplies)

Spain requires electronic invoicing in B2B transactions under Ley Crea y Crece once implementing regulations enter into force; large enterprises (over EUR 8 million annual turnover) will be required one year after the regulation enters into force and other businesses within two years, using the public Facturae format or equivalent interoperable format. For invoices to the public sector, electronic submission via FACe/e-Factura is currently mandatory. Large-regime Spanish taxpayers are subject to the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) real-time VAT records: invoice details are submitted to AEAT through public API web services within four calendar days of issuance/transaction. Veri*factu software rules require invoicing systems to generate tamper-evident QR codes and transmit truthful records; AEAT has no continuous central stamping for private B2B invoices, but SII provides de facto digital clearance for affected taxpayers.

AEAT may audit export zero-rating for four years from the return filing deadline. If the DUA, Bill of Lading, or remittance evidence is missing, false, or not contemporaneous, AEAT may treat the supply as taxable at 21% and issue an assessment for VAT, plus late-payment interest. The penalty ranges from 50% to 150% of the tax omitted under arts. 191 and 194 LGT, with aggravation to 150% where fraudulent means or false documentation are used. Forging an export declaration or using sham FX certificates may constitute tax fraud (Organic Law 10/1995 art. 305) and customs smuggling under Organic Law 12/1995, with criminal penalties and loss of fiscal good standing. AEAT may also claw back input VAT deducted on the non-existent export and deny VAT refunds for subsequent periods.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain operates the fully convertible euro. Both current-account flows (export settlements, royalties, fees, dividend distributions) and capital-account flows (equity injections, intercompany loans, M&A) are liberalised under Articles 63-65 TFEU and Law 19/2003, implementing Directive 88/361/EEC. There is no exchange-rate approval, no central-bank pre-clearance for remittances, and no profit-repatriation licensing hurdle; the only operational constraints are (i) EU/UN and national-security screening under Law 8/2020 for non-EU/EFTA investors acquiring 10% or more of a strategic biopharma/LNP-capacity target, (ii) statutory Balance-of-Payments statistical reporting to Banco de España for transactions above EUR 100,000, and (iii) tax-clearing obligations: dividend and cross-border income payments must be supported by residence certificates, beneficial-ownership declarations and, where treaty relief is invoked, a self-assessed withholding filing (Form 216) through the SOLRED system.

Export proceeds surrender rules

No surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio exist for export proceeds in Spain. Exporters freely retain receivables in EUR or foreign-currency accounts at authorised credit institutions, and there is no statutory conversion deadline. However, treasury must respect the Banco de España Balance-of-Payments informational regime: each export collection exceeding EUR 100,000 (or cumulated monthly flows passing the same threshold) must be reported to the Bank of Spain via the electronic statistical declaration, attaching the commercial invoice, customs Single Administrative Document (SAD/DUA), transport evidence and proof of settlement (MT103). Failure to report in time creates administrative sanction risk, not a currency-control restriction.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting within the European System of Central Banks, for banking and payment supervision; the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio / Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business) for foreign exchange, foreign investment registration and Balance-of-Payments declaration formalities under Law 19/2003, Law 8/2020 (FDI screening) and Royal Decree 664/1999.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH as ancillary collection and FX-conversion rails; LOW as sole or primary treasury banker. Spanish and EEA-passported Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) are licensed under Royal Decree-Law 19/2018 (EU E-Money Directive 2009/110/EC) and may provide payment accounts, card acquiring, currency conversion and outgoing/incoming MT103-equivalent rails, but they cannot take deposits, grant credit, release documentary letters of credit or issue guarantees. For a High_Risk_Special_License ISIC 2100 manufacturer (lipid nanoparticle encapsulation), most offshore digital EMIs will refuse onboarding because the sector is treated as pharma/high-risk; any viable fintech EMI (for example an EEA-licensed neobank with a Spanish branch) must be used only as a supplementary collection channel backed by a tier-1 fiduciary account; capital escrow, LC issuance and FX hedging must remain with a supervised credit institution.

Route all inbound equity and shareholder loans through TARGET2 via a tier-1 Spanish credit institution using a Spanish IBAN. Mechanics: (1) execute a board resolution authorising the capital contribution; (2) send SWIFT MT103 from the originator with the beneficiary Spanish IBAN/BIC and, if the investor is non-EU/EFTA, complete the Law 8/2020 pre-screening before control (10% or more) is achieved in the LNP/vaccine-adjuvant target; (3) classify the operation for Banco de España Balance-of-Payments purposes with the direct-investment purpose code (equity or intercompany debt) and file the applicable electronic declaration with the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores (DGCOMII) within the statutory deadline after completion; (4) verify the originator is an authorised credit institution and not a sanctioned or opaque corridor; (5) document the injection with the public deed of capital increase or notarial shareholder loan agreement. Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% general Corporate Income Tax rate. Newly incorporated entities carrying on an economic activity may qualify for a 15% rate during the first profitable tax period and the following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and conditions.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% Spanish withholding tax generally applies to dividends paid by a Spanish company to a non-resident recipient. The domestic participation exemption for qualifying EU or EEA parent companies may eliminate withholding where the minimum ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. An applicable tax treaty may reduce the rate, commonly to 5% to 15%, subject to treaty conditions and beneficial ownership.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Modelo 200 must generally be filed within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer ending on 31 December, the ordinary filing window is 1 to 25 July of the following year. Modelo 202 is generally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December; electronic payment deadlines may extend to the 15th day of those months.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December. Electronic payment authorization may be required earlier for direct-debit processing.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: EUR 250,000 per related person or entity, measured by transaction type and at arm's-length value, is a principal threshold for the general exemption from Spanish related-party documentation, subject to statutory exceptions. Documentation requirements may also depend on taxpayer size, group status, transaction nature, and whether the transaction involves tax havens or specified high-risk categories. Spanish Local File and Master File requirements should be tested separately; large multinational groups may additionally have Country-by-Country Reporting obligations where consolidated group revenue meets the EUR 750 million threshold.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a single standalone Economic Substance Regulation regime equivalent to certain offshore ESR systems. Substance is nevertheless material under the Spanish General Anti-Avoidance Rule, conflict-in-the-application doctrine, beneficial-ownership analysis, EU anti-abuse rules, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, treaty anti-abuse provisions, and principal-purpose testing. The Spanish SL should maintain genuine personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or controlled production infrastructure, decision-making in Spain, commercial risk assumption, technical and regulatory functions, appropriate capitalization, real research or manufacturing activity, and contemporaneous records. A foreign parent should not receive dividends, royalties, interest, or service fees merely as a conduit without commercial function and decision-making capacity.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax evasion and fraudulent Corporate Income Tax reporting

Statutory sanction: Administrative tax penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax or improperly obtained refund. Where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax period, criminal tax fraud may arise, with imprisonment generally from one to five years and a fine from one to six times the amount defrauded; aggravated cases may carry higher penalties.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur civil liability for negligent or deliberate management, derivative liability for certain unpaid tax debts, and criminal liability where they participate in the offense. Courts may order restitution, fines, disqualification from public office or management, and imprisonment. Travel restrictions are exceptional and depend on judicial proceedings, flight risk, and court orders; they are not an automatic consequence of a tax assessment.
False invoicing and accounting manipulation

Statutory sanction: Tax penalties may apply for improper deductions, failure to substantiate transactions, and fraudulent bookkeeping. Conduct may also constitute document forgery, accounting crime, or tax fraud, with criminal fines and imprisonment depending on the facts and amounts involved.

Director personal liability: Directors, finance officers, and beneficial owners who authorize or knowingly facilitate false records may face criminal prosecution, civil restitution, asset seizure, management disqualification, and imprisonment. Corporate limited liability does not protect individuals from their own criminal conduct.
Transfer pricing manipulation

Statutory sanction: The Spanish tax authority may make a primary adjustment, impose documentation and valuation penalties, assess late-payment interest, and apply secondary adjustments treating the benefit as a dividend or contribution. Failure to provide required documentation may generate transaction-based penalties, subject to statutory caps.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil liability where they approve materially unsupported arrangements or conceal the true beneficiary. Criminal liability generally requires intentional participation in tax fraud or another offense; ordinary pricing disagreement alone does not create imprisonment or travel-ban exposure.
Improper dividend, interest, or royalty repatriation

Statutory sanction: The Spanish SL may be assessed for unpaid withholding tax, interest, and withholding-related penalties. Treaty or EU relief may be denied, and the payment may be recharacterized for Corporate Income Tax and withholding purposes.

Director personal liability: Directors may be jointly or subsidiarily liable in serious cases involving deliberate withholding failures, concealment, or asset stripping. Criminal exposure requires facts meeting applicable criminal thresholds and proof of personal participation.
Shell company, conduit, and beneficial-ownership abuse

Statutory sanction: Benefits may be denied under anti-abuse rules, and transactions may be recharacterized. Tax assessments, withholding liabilities, interest, penalties, and denial of deductions may follow. EU and treaty relief may be refused under principal-purpose, beneficial-ownership, or general anti-abuse principles.

Director personal liability: Individuals who knowingly create or operate conduit structures may face civil liability, tax derivation, asset seizure, and criminal liability where tax fraud, money laundering, forgery, or another offense is established. Travel restrictions and imprisonment require judicial action and are not automatic.
Money laundering and suspicious financial flows

Statutory sanction: Spanish anti-money-laundering breaches may result in substantial administrative fines, public or private sanctions, suspension, management disqualification, and reporting to competent authorities. Money laundering may constitute a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment and fines, with aggravated consequences for professional or organized conduct.

Director personal liability: Directors, compliance officers, beneficial owners, and facilitators may face personal criminal liability, confiscation, civil restitution, management disqualification, and court-ordered travel restrictions or imprisonment where statutory conditions are met.
VAT, customs, and intra-EU reporting failure

Statutory sanction: Additional VAT, customs duty, interest, and administrative penalties may arise. Serious customs fraud may create criminal exposure, forfeiture, and seizure of goods. Incorrect Intrastat or recapitulative statements may generate separate penalties.

Director personal liability: Directors and customs representatives may be liable for knowingly false declarations or fraudulent import arrangements. Criminal liability depends on intent, value, concealment, and participation.
Unlicensed pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or regulated manufacturing activity

Statutory sanction: Regulatory authorities may impose fines, suspend or revoke authorizations, order product seizure or destruction, prohibit operations, and initiate criminal proceedings for serious public-health violations. Tax deductions and incentives may be challenged where expenditure relates to unlawful activity.

Director personal liability: Directors may face administrative sanctions, civil claims for product harm, and criminal liability for intentional or grossly negligent conduct causing public-health risk. Corporate form does not shield directors from personal regulatory or criminal responsibility.
Failure to maintain statutory books and tax records

Statutory sanction: The tax authority may reject deductions and credits, apply recordkeeping penalties, use indirect assessment methods, and impose late-filing or information-reporting penalties. Audit limitation periods may be extended where concealment or obstruction exists.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur civil liability for negligent governance and may face personal sanctions where they obstruct an inspection, destroy records, or knowingly submit false information. Criminal liability requires additional statutory elements.
Asset stripping and creditor prejudice

Statutory sanction: Transactions may be challenged or rescinded, and directors may face insolvency-related liability, tax derivation, clawback claims, and disqualification from administering third-party assets.

Director personal liability: Directors may be ordered to cover insolvency shortfalls, return improperly transferred assets, compensate creditors, and bear civil or criminal consequences for fraudulent insolvency. Courts may impose management disqualification and, where criminal conduct is proven, fines or imprisonment.
Sanctions, export-control, and dual-use violations

Statutory sanction: Violations may lead to transaction blocking, asset freezing, administrative fines, license revocation, confiscation, and criminal prosecution under applicable Spanish, European Union, and international sanctions regimes.

Director personal liability: Directors and compliance personnel may face personal administrative or criminal liability where they knowingly approve, facilitate, or recklessly ignore prohibited transactions. Asset freezes, travel restrictions, disqualification, and imprisonment may follow a competent authority's or court's order.
